I think the tendency is to treat everything as a serious mental problem and coddle people, when in reality I think the majority of people in the situation could do with a swift kick in the pants and some guidance. People need to be able to solve things for themselves. That's where the battle needs to be fought anyway! The person has to change. Nobody can do it for them! That's why my philosophy is to give them the tools and nudge them along. We can't stay children forever. The right knowledge put into practice can go a long way towards helping someone conquer their fears and phobias. Knowledge is power. Ignorance is slavery. We have to face our problems and fears, not hide from them in a perpetual state of helplessness, and I think helplessness has too often become associated with the label of "disorder".

edit: And one more thing. Fear isn't necessarily bad. I'm afraid of becoming fat too. It keeps me honest with myself. It motivates me. The thing about me is though is that I went out and learned what I needed to make sure I got fit and stayed that way. That knowledge and experience has helped me greatly lessen my fear. We are a naturally curious and intelligent species. We conquer by learning.
